📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that september ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud tech giant CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

Sources indicate that recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee mentioned CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

It has been revealed that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

It has been revealed that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and latest markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

In a recent development, in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he stated.

Industry observers note that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Industry observers note that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

According to recent reports, overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the manufacturer if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," mentioned Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia (NVDA -0.90%) has a handful of problems right now.
  • In a recent development, however, let's take a moment and assess the tech giant for what it is right now.
  • If that happens, investors need to know what's going on with its core business, and seeing what it just noted regarding its future should make investors bullish on the stock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Nvidia (NVDA -0.90%) has a handful of problems right now. Although its chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, is back in his former position, there are still questions about his activities and whether any of Nvidia's technology or products made their way into China's hands unlawfully. There are risks here, and the market has certainly priced those into the stock.

In a recent development, however, let's take a moment and assess the tech giant for what it is right now. It's entirely possible that all of this turns out to be nothing and Nvidia is slapped with a couple-billion-dollar fine that it easily pays and moves on with.

If that happens, investors need to know what's going on with its core business, and seeing what it just noted regarding its future should make investors bullish on the stock.

According to recent reports, in Q3, Nvidia's revenue rose an impressive 103% year over year to $116 billion. Few companies ever double their revenue year over year, and even fewer ever cross the $100 billion revenue mark. Nobody besides Nvidia has ever combined these two feats, and that tells investors just how incredible its business is.

To end the year, it expects $130 billion in quarterly revenue. That's an impressive figure in itself, but Nvidia is known to undershoot projections and overdeliver. It did that in Q3, as it projected only $108 billion in Q3 revenue at the end of Q2. If Nvidia beats by a similar percentage, its revenue could approach $140 billion during Q4. That would result in its quarter-over-quarter growth rate reaching 21%. That's a significant deal because it reveals that Nvidia's growth is staying steady.

NVDA Revenue (QoQ Growth) data by YCharts.

Next year, Nvidia expects revenue to rise at a 75% clip, up from the 70% growth projected at the end of Q2. That would put Nvidia's annual revenue well above $700 billion. Combined with its profitability, that would easily make it the highest-earning tech giant on earth. With Nvidia's track record of beating expectations, the real growth figure could be far higher than this, and lead to downright incredible growth for a company of Nvidia's size.

In Nvidia's Q3 report, it also unveiled a $150 billion increase to the share repurchase authorization. If it grows as it expects to for the rest of 2026 and 2027, that figure could get raised significantly, too. During Q3, Nvidia generated about $44 billion in free cash flow; if that increases alongside its revenue, Nvidia could start putting a ton of its cash to work repurchasing shares during the next few years. If Nvidia starts buying back its stock in even larger quantities, it will boost its earnings per share figure. This action is being made even more effective by Nvidia's relatively cheap stock price.

Sources indicate that nvidia trades for less than 14 times trailing earnings, which is well below its recent average. With Nvidia growing at a rapid pace, this price tag just doesn't make sense if its troubles are solved regarding exports.

That's still a large risk with Nvidia, but if it were a major problem, there would be upper management resigning at Nvidia and Huang likely wouldn't have come back. His willingness to come back as CEO and testify to Congress conveys that this risk is relatively minor for the stock.

Industry observers note that the artificial intelligence (AI) arms race is far from over, and it could be several years before spending tops out. With the market pricing in a major downturn in AI spending in 2027 (despite what every firm in the sector has said), now is the perfect opportunity to pounce on Nvidia's cheap stock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A one-line prompt that makes ChatGPT leak its private opinion of you, in a pretty funny format: a WhatsApp group chat where the AI models gossip about their users.

Also worth trying on Claude, Gemini, or any assistant that's been accumulating your chat history.

According to recent reports, instead of a summary, the model commits to the bit. It invents a group chat, something like "Consumers We Can't Figure Out", puts the other AI models in it, and lets them gossip. About you. Using everything it has quietly learned from your conversations.

One person's actual output, shared with permission. Translated from Turkish; his name and a few identifying details have been swapped for generic ones. Everything else is exactly as the model wrote it.

Shared by its author, translated from Turkish, with his name and identifying details generalized. The "recursion, no base case" line is doing a lot of work here.

Run the prompt, read your leaked group chat, and notice two things: how hard you laugh, and how much of it is true. Both measurements are the point.

Industry observers note that I'm not affiliated with OpenAI and this may indeed be a viral marketing idea they're testing. But I had such a laugh, I figured others would have some fun with it as well and decided to share it.

Big contracts with Anthropic and Alphabet are primed to play big roles in driving that growth.

SpaceX has quickly become a powerhouse in the AI compute services category. The company has a contract to provide $920 million a month in AI compute to Alphabet over a 33-month period, working out to a $30 billion deal. It also has a compute deal with Anthropic that's set to ramp up to its full value of $3.1 billion per month this December and potentially extend through 2029 -- working out to a max contract value of $120.5 billion. While the Anthropic deal includes guaranteed provisioning that expires in the first quarter and the option for either party to back out with a 90-day notice, the contract is effectively locked in for the period due to the notice requirements.

AI has become the tech giant's most important growth driver, and securing contract renewals would be a strong indicator for the company's competitive viability and long-term growth opportunities in the space. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

In a recent development, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," stated Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he remarked.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone mentioned.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That stated, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

"There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, stated Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Recent findings suggest that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

According to recent reports, the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, mentioned Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

It has been revealed that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he noted. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In a recent development, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

Sources indicate that "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

Sources indicate that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

It has been revealed that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, noted R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo remarked.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he mentioned. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

There are few settings more pulse-quickening than a battlefield, a fact that director and co-writer Peter Berg taps into for this post-Pearl Harbor war thriller.

Based on the 2022 Buzz Bissinger non-fiction novel "The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II," the story follows four American college football players—played by Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson, and Tom Francis—who enlist in the Marine Corps and, to momentarily forget about the brutal horrors of being on the front lines, participate in a Christmas Eve football match ahead of the Battle of Okinawa.

Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
  • During the keynote for the firm’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella unveiled Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
  • Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the firm’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella unveiled Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft noted. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also revealed Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

In a recent development, “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

It has been revealed that the firm added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

It has been revealed that nadella also confirmed a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up rapidly,” Microsoft stated of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

According to recent reports, microsoft also unveiled that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can swiftly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft revealed a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft confirmed last year, is the firm’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

Recent findings suggest that “It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise aims.

10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

Industry observers note that it's been a record-breaking year for Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.04%)(BRKB +0.32%) in more ways than one. Despite Warren Buffett retiring as CEO at the end of last year, his successor, Greg Abel, has led the organization's shares to an all-time high.

Even though Abel completely overhauled Berkshire's $346 billion investment portfolio in the first quarter, one common thread between Berkshire's current and former bosses remains the same: portfolio concentration. Both Buffett and Abel strongly believe in wagering big on their best ideas. As of the closing bell on Nov. 20, 47% of Berkshire's invested assets ($162.6 billion) were put to work in three proven winners: Apple (AAPL +1.00%), American Express (AXP +1.38%), and Coca-Cola (KO -0.23%).

Industry observers note that greg Abel now oversees Berkshire's investment portfolio following Warren Buffett's retirement. Image source: Getty Images.

If there's a theme among all three of these stocks, it's that they were all built up by the Oracle of Omaha. Warren Buffett began buying shares of Apple in the first quarter of 2016, eventually building a nearly 944.3-million-share position at its peak in 2020.

Buffett's lure with Apple was its extremely loyal customer base and its exceptional pricing power.

NASDAQ · As of 10:44 AM ET 11/27/26.

It has been revealed that furthermore, Apple has executed the largest nominal share repurchase program on Wall Street. Through the end of Apple's fiscal 2026 (ending Sept. 26), the tech giant has repurchased $902.8 billion of its common stock, retiring nearly 45% of its outstanding shares in the process.

But it's Apple's innovative prowess that entices Greg Abel. Under Tim Cook, who stepped down as CEO on Sept. 1, the manufacturer shifted to higher-margin subscription services and launched its generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform, Apple Intelligence.

Credit-services provider American Express (Amex) is Berkshire Hathaway's second-longest holding (since 1991) and was labeled an "indefinite" position by Warren Buffett in his 2023 letter to shareholders.

NYSE · As of 10:42 AM ET 11/27/26.

According to recent reports, amex benefits from being cyclical and tackling both sides of the transaction counter. It's the third-largest payment processor in the U.S. by credit-card-network purchase volume, meaning it collects sizable merchant fees to facilitate transactions. It's also a lender, generating annual fees and interest income from its cardholders (businesses and individuals). Given that economic expansions last considerably longer than recessions, being able to double-dip works in Amex's favor more often than not.

Additionally, Amex has historically attracted well-to-do clientele. High earners are less likely to alter their spending habits or fail to pay their bills than the average-earning worker, allowing Amex to bounce back from economic downturns faster than most other lenders.

No stock in Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio has been held longer than Coca-Cola (since 1988). Thanks to Berkshire's minuscule cost basis in Coca-Cola and the latter's 64-year streak of raising its dividend, Abel's company is netting a 65% annual yield on cost from this position.

Recent findings suggest that coca-Cola's long-term outperformance stems from its well-known brand name and global reach. With the exception of North Korea, Cuba, and Russia, it has operations in every country. This allows it to generate organic growth in emerging markets while reaping the steady reward of predictable operating cash flow in developed countries.

NYSE · As of 10:43 AM ET 11/27/26.

According to recent reports, the argument can also be made that Coca-Cola's marketing is unrivaled. The manufacturer's holiday tie-ins, coupled with its use of AI in social media marketing campaigns, help it cross generational gaps and connect with consumers of all ages.

Industry observers note that the iPhone 17 was arguably one of the biggest upgrades Apple gave its base iPhone in years. And even though the iPhone 18 Pro series is now here, I still think the iPhone 17 is the phone most people should buy if they're looking to get an iPhone this year.

Thanks to a Black Friday iPhone 17 deal at Metro by T-Mobile, you can now get one for just $729, saving you $200 without trading in your old phone.

The iPhone 17 may be over a year old at this point, but there's still a lot to like about this phone. One of the biggest upgrades Apple introduced with this generation was the 6.3-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate. Apple had previously reserved 120Hz refresh rates for its Pro models, but bringing it to the standard iPhone 17 gave people one less reason to spend extra on a Pro model.

Industry observers note that and while the A19 chipset is no longer Apple's latest, it's still more than capable of handling pretty much anything you'd want to do on your iPhone. Moreover, unlike the previous base model iPhones, you also get 256GB base storage with the iPhone 17, so you don't necessarily need to spend extra on a higher storage variant.

In our iPhone 17 review, we described the phone as offering "better upgrades than the Pros." The phone also lasted 12 hours and 47 minutes in our battery life test, which should be enough to get most people through a day of regular use.

There is one thing worth keeping in mind with the Metro deal, though. The iPhone will remain locked to the carrier for at least 365 days after activation, meaning you won't be able to use another carrier's SIM or eSIM during that period. If you frequently travel internationally and rely on travel eSIMs, you might be better off buying an unlocked iPhone.

Industry observers note that get the unlocked 256GB iPhone 17 directly from Apple for $929 and receive a $75 Apple Gift Card through November 30. Select "Connect on your own later" to avoid committing to a specific carrier.

Sources indicate that apple is also running its own Black Friday promotion through November 30. You can purchase the unlocked 256GB iPhone 17 for $929 by selecting the "Connect on your own later" option and receive a $75 Apple Gift Card.

Sure, it's not an upfront discount like the Metro by T-Mobile deal, but it's definitely worth considering if you're also planning to buy AirPods or an Apple Watch. You're essentially saving $75 on your next Apple purchase while getting a fully unlocked iPhone 17 without switching carriers.

According to recent reports, I still think the iPhone 17 is the iPhone most people should be looking at this year. Unless you specifically want the more advanced cameras or some of the newer hardware on the iPhone 18 Pro, there's not much you're missing out on. And if you're already considering switching to a prepaid carrier, Metro's $200 discount makes it an even better buy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Recent findings suggest that health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround proposal.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

It has been revealed that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the manufacturer's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the organization's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

It has been revealed that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Recent findings suggest that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it confirms its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

In a recent development, heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

It has been revealed that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active people in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

In a recent development, "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently rolled out Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the tech giant's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

According to recent reports, morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

The five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

Industry observers note that while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft notes its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI stated it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

According to recent reports, “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Firm to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft mentioned it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman mentioned during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the organization has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Industry observers note that western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman mentioned of the latest coding model the company revealed at Ignite.

According to recent reports, the organization also released its latest image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. It has been revealed that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:20AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Bill Ackman and his team at Pershing Square, the parent company of the investment manager Pershing Square Capital Management, run a concentrated portfolio. Ackman is not afraid to play contrarian, and he isn't afraid to hold stocks long term, which is a different strategy from that employed by most standard hedge funds.

In a recent development, ackman has also purchased stakes in several hyperscalers driving the artificial intelligence revolution. Given Pershing's impressive track record and Ackman's huge following, investors are always curious about what the billionaire is buying.

In the third quarter, Ackman and his team continued to load up on one tech stock that's down by about 44% over the past year. Does he know something Wall Street doesn't?

Sources indicate that bill Ackman. Image source: Getty Images.

Nearly all sectors have been disrupted by the emergence of artificial intelligence, even companies that were considered cutting-edge tech stocks very recently. The video streaming business faces threats too. Investors are now concerned about lower barriers to entry for content creation, as well as the rising popularity of short-form content from platforms like YouTube.

Industry observers note that these concerns have spooked investors about the outlook for streaming giant Netflix (NFLX +2.19%). The stock, which hit an all-time high in June 2025, has been crushed over the past year.

Reports of declining viewer engagement have led many to believe an industrywide shift is underway, and Netflix's management team more or less acknowledged those concerns on its Q3 earnings call last month.

"Turning to the U.S., the other region, our engagement is solid, and it will allow us to continue to grow as we have for the last several years," co-CEO Greg Peters noted on the call. "We know that we can do better, and that better is our upside.".

Sources indicate that while Ackman and Pershing had previously owned a stake in Netflix several years ago, they closed it. Then, they opened a fresh position in the second quarter of 2026. In Q3, Pershing increased that position by 18%; as of the end of the quarter, Netflix made up 3.5% of the portfolio.

In its June interim report, Pershing mentioned that it believes investors are underestimating the cost of creating long-form, high-quality content, which it said remains "among the most compute-intensive tasks." Pershing also noted that the popularity of short-form content has had no significant effect on Netflix's results.

NASDAQ · As of 10:42 AM ET 11/27/26.

In a recent development, in Pershing's Q3 patch earlier this month, the company reiterated its belief in Netflix and mentioned investors are focusing too much on engagement as measured by viewer watch time. It believes the company's foray into live programming and other fresh content will make this less of a concern.

Pershing is also excited about Netflix's advertising business.

According to recent reports, "Advertising revenue continues to scale rapidly, and the lower-priced ad-supported tier is meaningfully expanding Netflix's addressable market," Pershing wrote. "AI should further enhance the business by improving content recommendation and ad targeting algorithms, driving efficiencies and enabling new forms of interactive and personalized content.".

Pershing believes Netflix can generate double-digit percentage revenue growth over the next few years, while compounding earnings at 20% annually.

There's no question that the rise of short-form content poses a challenge for companies like Netflix, which, once upon a time, may not have considered short form as a competitor.

I agree with Ackman and his team that the market may be underestimating how difficult it is to replicate high-quality, long-form content with cheaper new technologies. I still think that is evident whether you look at successful Netflix reveals or at long-form podcasts that continue to do well. Netflix has also raised subscription prices across all its tiers and continues to see healthy retention, according to management.

Netflix will likely need to invest in new types of content and keep adjusting its strategy to stay ahead in the entertainment space, but the company has the expertise and resources to do so. AI can also help advance and optimize its existing business.

While nobody knows exactly how AI and short-form content will continue to affect the streaming video space, I like the risk-reward proposition here.

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

After reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-fresh device? (You’ve been warned.).

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

According to recent reports, the compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

In a recent development, the Duo is a great gift for someone who’s remarked they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV highlights on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

According to recent reports, the iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

It has been revealed that the Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

It has been revealed that perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

In a recent development, it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Industry observers note that like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

Recent findings suggest that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

Industry observers note that the Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, anthropic (ANT +8.67%) raised a record amount of capital with its initial public offering (IPO).
  • The offering’s underwriters exercised their greenshoe option, buying an extra 147 million shares for just over $12 billion.
  • According to recent reports, but Anthropic's public offering accounted for only about 6% of its fully diluted share count, which includes stock options, restricted stock units, and convertible notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Levy – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:24AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

In a recent development, anthropic (ANT +8.67%) raised a record amount of capital with its initial public offering (IPO). It sold 980 million shares to the public at $83 each, raising about $81 billion.

The offering’s underwriters exercised their greenshoe option, buying an extra 147 million shares for just over $12 billion. The AI lab also raised $26 billion in concurrent private placement deals with several big tech companies alongside its IPO. All in all, that brought the company $119.5 billion before underwriting expenses.

According to recent reports, but Anthropic's public offering accounted for only about 6% of its fully diluted share count, which includes stock options, restricted stock units, and convertible notes. The rest of the shares — those held by insiders and pre-IPO stakeholders — remain locked up. But the expiration of the first phase of that lock-up comes in just a few weeks on Dec. 15.

There are some important details investors should know before the first lock-up expiration.

According to recent reports, anthropic's valuation at its IPO was about $1.5 trillion. Given that massive market cap, staggering its lock-up expiration helps prevent a flood of shares from weighing down the stock price. Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +3.63%) is taking a similar approach with its IPO lock-up.

According to recent reports, anthropic outlined its lock-up expiration calendar in its prospectus. Of note, Anthropic has two share classes: Class A shares are ordinary shares of capital stock; Class N shares are those that were issued to strategic investors, such as tech companies investing in its private placement offerings. Class N shares convert to Class A shares upon sale to unaffiliated parties.

A huge number of shares are set to be added to the stock’s float — the pool of tradable shares — over the next year. The current float is set to double with the first four lock-up expirations between December and February, and it'll increase by another 70% from there after Anthropic's first earnings report as a publicly traded manufacturer.

Those early lock-up expirations will be a major test of just how much appetite there is for Anthropic shares. SpaceX faced similar dynamics. While the first expiration went well, with the market fully absorbing the new shares without much impact on the price, its more recent lock-up expirations haven't gone as smoothly for shareholders.

Another important detail about Anthropic's share lockup that you might notice is that Class N share lockups are backloaded. That's because shareholders with more than a 0.5% ownership stake are subject to the full 365-day lockup period, while smaller shareholders will be able to sell all of their stock after 180 days.

The 0.5%-plus ownership group includes names like Alphabet and Amazon. They'll likely seek to reduce their market influence on the stock price until they can sell all their shares.

In a recent development, the big fear for investors is that a flood of newly tradable shares will increase selling pressure on the stock, sending the price lower as Anthropic’s early investors and employees look to cash out. Indeed, that's the whole reason why Anthropic scheduled a much more spaced-out lock-up schedule than the typical IPO.

Recent findings suggest that while the increase in float could push the stock price down, investors know these selling events are coming. That could lead them to discount shares ahead of key lock-up expiration dates, making it easier for the market to absorb sellers.

It has been revealed that that's exactly what we saw with SpaceX. Shares actually climbed 6% on the date of its first lock-up expiration.

NASDAQ · As of 10:45 AM ET 11/27/26.

According to recent reports, over time, Anthropic's share price moves should more closely reflect changes in the business's value. Short-term selling pressure from lock-up expirations could provide discounts that long-term investors can take advantage of to build their positions.

But investors shouldn't take an unlock-related sell-off in Anthropic shares as a good reason to buy the stock. There are considerable risks for the AI stock that need to be factored into even the rosiest outlooks for the company. If you don't buy it with a wide enough margin of safety, you could face some significant losses if your forecast proves too optimistic. Determining the price you're willing to pay for the stock before a potential selling event can help you capitalize on the potential opportunity it creates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.

Sources indicate that the partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

In a recent development, now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies mentioned. They proposal to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber plans to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

In a recent development, “Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an notable milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, mentioned in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro claims it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

Industry observers note that in May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the firm the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

According to recent reports, the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

It’s been a big year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has introduced investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

Sources indicate that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Industry observers note that also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid prepares, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Sources indicate that gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

Recent findings suggest that at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

It has been revealed that AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Industry observers note that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

Industry observers note that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US consumers can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The upcoming landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

It has been revealed that “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release stated. Google’s newly introduced Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a latest and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful fresh features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

It has been revealed that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

A fresh feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a new feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

In a recent development, the upcoming app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the newly introduced Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the newly introduced features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone customers. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

I was part of the wider testing panel for the Siena Signature, and while I was impressed with its high-quality design, it's definitely not for everyone. However, a recent price drop means it's one of the best value Black Friday mattress deals happening live.

I've decided to pit the Siena Signature against the SweetNight CoolNest and the EGOHOME Black memory foam mattresses. With this in-depth SweetNight CoolNest vs Siena Signature vs EGOHOME Black comparison guide, you can decide which budget bed in the Black Friday mattress sales is right for you.

Side and back sleepers; cooling.

All three mattresses make an appearance in our bests cheap mattress guide, as they all meet key criteria: they're under $400 for a queen and they outperform their budget price.

As for benefits, the Siena takes home gold. While EGOHOME and SweetNight offer a 100-night sleep trial, free shipping and a 10-year mattress warranty with their mattress purchases, Siena offers a 180-night sleep trial and free returns (in addition to a 10-year warranty and free shipping).

However, you can now snag free pillows worth $89.99 with your mattress purcchase. Whenever or wherever you buy, you're guaranteed free shipping, a 10-year warranty and 100-night sleep trial.

The Siena Signature is $279 for a queen, which is a step up from its standard deal price of $329 for a queen. While a twin was $199, the new discount also takes a twin down to $169. Benefits include free shipping and returns, a 180-night sleep trial and a 10-year warranty.

Recent findings suggest that use EGOHOME code EARLYBF15 to take a queen EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress from $379 (MSRP:$559) down to $330.65, which is better than last week's deal when it was an extra 10% off and $341.10 for a queen. You can also receive a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial.

Sources indicate that thanks to their all-foam layers, the Siena Signature and the SweetNight CoolNest both appear in best memory foam mattress guide (as our best cooling and best soft pick respectively). The EGOHOME Black 12" Foam Mattress is also made entirely of foam.

The SweetNight is 12" tall and features the most sophisticated design of the three, with six internal layers of foam. One layer is infused with cooling Phase Change Material (PCM), which has been proven to improve human heat dissipation by up to 25.6% compared with non-cooling mattresses, and the mattress itself is encased in a cool-to-the-touch knit cover.

The Siena Signature is the shortest at 10" tall, and has the simplest design with just two internal layers: one layer of memory foam for comfort and one stability foam layer for support. These layers of topped by a soft, breathable cover.

While the EGOHOME Black Foam has the same 12" height as the SweetNight CoolNest, it has half as many layers. These layers are enveloped in a graphene-infused cover for both temperature and moisture control.

I conducted hands-on testing on the Siena Signature Mattress, following our thorough mattress methodology. I also lab-tested the CoolNest and the EGOHOME Black, in addition to sleeping on them at home for subjective feedback.

I'm a side and back sleeper, and I loved sleeping on the CoolNest during my SweetNight CoolNest mattress review. It balanced medium-firm support and body-cradling comfort well, and the wider testing panel agreed that it has the right amount of pressure relief for side and back sleeping.

However, my fellow testers and I agreed that it isn't firm enough for stomach sleepers, even if is one of the best mattresses for side sleepers. Still, its responsive feel is great for moving around and switching sleep positions without feeling "stuck" in the mattress' foam.

The Siena Signature, on the other hand, is one of the best mattress for stomach sleepers. When I was part of the hands-on testing panel for the Siena Signature, the moment I felt this firm memory foam bed I immediately knew it offered tons of support — and that it was too firm for a side sleeper like me to test meaningfully.

Instead, a front-sleeping tester became the lead tester for our Siena Signature review, and she loved the lumbar support it offered to her preferred sleep style.

Sources indicate that for my EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress review, I slept on the EGOHOME mattress for over seven months (for reference, we usually test mattresses at-home for three weeks), and I always felt supported no matter what position I slept in. However, the wider testing panel (along with our subjective tests) found that its body-hugging foam is great for side and back sleepers, but too soft for stomach sleepers.

Both the Siena Signature and the SweetNight CoolNest performed surprisingly well in our temperature regulation tests, where we used a thermal imaging camera to measure how well the mattresses absorb and dissipate heat.

As one of the best cooling mattresses on the market, the SweetNight has a rapid cooling rate of 2.1°F per minute. The Siena, meanwhile, displayed a slower cooling rate of 1.52°F per minute; however, it absorbed less heat in the first place.

Subjectively, too, the SweetNight wins, as my fellow testers and I were immediately impressed with its cool-to-the-touch feel. I also slept on it during summer heatwaves in a building with no AC, and I never felt overheated.

The Siena also kept its lead tester comfortable, but provided a temperature-neutral feel rather than an actively cooling feel — this may be because it's designed with a focus on breathability rather than featuring any specific cooling tech.

It has been revealed that in contrast, the EGOHOME Black didn't impress me with its cooling when I slept on it during hot weather. I often woke up feeling overheated and could feel patches of heat build up under my pressure points. Testing panelist Ruth Jones, agreed, reporting that she felt the mattress warm up when she was lying on her stomach.

✅ You want a dedicated cooling bed: While the Siena Signature's temperature control was also impressive, the cool-to-the-touch SweetNight CoolNest features advanced cooling tech.

✅ You sleep on your side: It provides a contouring feel that's great for side sleepers, but it's responsive enough to support back sleepers and avoid the "quicksand" feel associated with memory foam.

✅ You need firm support: If you're a back or stomach sleeper, then the Siena Signature's firmness with keep your hips and lower back upright to prevent back pain.

✅ You want the cheapest option: At just $279 for a queen (and starting at $169) and offering the longest sleep trial, the Siena Signature boasts the best value for money.

✅ You want a classic memory foam feel: The EGOHOME Black 12" Foam provides a body-hugging "sink-in" feel that's traditionally associated with memory foam beds.

✅ You're a side or back sleeper: The EGOHOME has a medium-firm feel that molds to side sleeper's pressure points but also support back sleepers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:28AM EST.
  • Sources indicate that if you're turning 65 in 2027, you'll soon be signing up for Medicare, and of course, you'll have the option to claim Social Security, too, assuming you're not already receiving checks.
  • Here are three things you should be aware of before you apply for Social Security and Medicare in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:28AM EST.

Sources indicate that if you're turning 65 in 2027, you'll soon be signing up for Medicare, and of course, you'll have the option to claim Social Security, too, assuming you're not already receiving checks. But these are major financial decisions, so it's worth thinking them through carefully before you decide.

Here are three things you should be aware of before you apply for Social Security and Medicare in 2027.

You are within your rights to claim Social Security at age 65, but doing so is technically considered early claiming and carries an early withdrawal penalty. To avoid this, you must delay your Social Security application until your full retirement age (FRA). This is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later. Older adults have slightly younger FRAs.

This doesn't mean you shouldn't claim Social Security at 65. It can still be the right move for you if you aren't able to work, have little personal savings, or have a short life expectancy.

In a recent development, but if you don't need your checks right now, you might get a larger lifetime benefit by waiting a few more years before you apply. If you'd like, you can continue delaying Social Security until you qualify for your largest benefit at age 70.

Sources indicate that when you're on both Medicare and Social Security benefits, the government withholds your Medicare Part B premiums from your Social Security checks. This gives you one less bill to worry about each month.

In 2027, the Part B premium will be $209.40 for most seniors, though wealthy Americans will pay more. If you opt to claim Social Security later, you will have to pay these premiums out of your own pocket until you apply for Social Security.

There's no rule saying that you must apply for Social Security and Medicare at the same time. Choose your Social Security claiming age based on your estimated life expectancy, finances, and personal preferences. Consider a variety of claiming ages before you settle on one to make sure you're comfortable with the trade-offs of your decision.

Warren Buffett Wrote in February 2009 That He Buys Stocks Like Socks, When They're Marked Down. The S&P 500 Gained 50% During the Next Year.
