Latest Update: The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.
  • In a recent development, spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
  • “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

In a recent development, spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

“It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite launches, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the tech giant’s IPO in June.

“You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk mentioned in March.

Sources indicate that on its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It says that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

Sources indicate that space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

Industry observers note that it’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

“We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that rolled out last year in total.

Industry observers note that scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center plan would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

It has been revealed that “There are scientific papers out there raising challenges,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (479 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Don't Need Your RMDs? Why Investing Them Could Be Your Smartest Move Yet

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (479 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you have a pile of money sitting in a traditional retirement account, you can't just leave it untouched forever, even if you don't need it and would rather pass it along to your heirs.
  • Industry observers note that RMDs apply to traditional retirement accounts starting at age 73 or 75, depending on your year of birth.
  • Converting a traditional IRA or 401(k) to a Roth IRA before RMDs begin could solve the problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Maurie Backman – Nov 27, 2026 at 6:36AM EST.

If you have a pile of money sitting in a traditional retirement account, you can't just leave it untouched forever, even if you don't need it and would rather pass it along to your heirs. Contributions to accounts like traditional IRAs and 401(k)s are made on a pre-tax basis. But the IRS eventually wants its cut. That's where required minimum distributions (RMDs) come in.

Industry observers note that RMDs apply to traditional retirement accounts starting at age 73 or 75, depending on your year of birth. And they can be a huge hassle from a tax perspective.

Converting a traditional IRA or 401(k) to a Roth IRA before RMDs begin could solve the problem. But not everyone is a candidate for a Roth conversion, and you may not be able to do one in full.

If you're stuck taking RMDs you don't need, all isn't lost, though. One savvy move on your part could help turn an otherwise annoying situation into an opportunity.

Industry observers note that while the IRS might force you to take money out of your retirement account, it can't force you to spend it. If you don't need your RMDs, investing them in a taxable brokerage account could be a solid move, especially if your goal is to leave behind a sizable inheritance.

Under current federal tax rules, inherited taxable investment assets generally receive a stepped-up cost basis to their fair market value upon the original owner's date of death. So let's say you invest $100,000 of RMDs since you don't need the money to cover your costs. If that $100,000 grows to be worth $200,000, your heirs could inherit your taxable brokerage account at a $200,000 cost basis.

If your heirs then immediately sell those assets, they shouldn't owe capital gains taxes. And if they wait to sell, they'll only owe capital gains taxes on appreciation that happens after your passing.

People with large legacy goals often focus on Roth conversions, since inheriting a Roth IRA can be more advantageous than inheriting a traditional IRA. But if a Roth conversion doesn't make sense for you, consider investing your RMDs in a taxable account and earmarking them for your loved ones.

You'll still have to deal with taxes on your RMDs if you go this route. But you could end up sparing your heirs a major tax headache down the line in return.

Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

Once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response noted, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

It has been revealed that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Fresh York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news.
  • According to recent reports, we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired.
  • Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news. One of the best free options for organizing your work and home life is reaching the end of its life. Microsoft looks to retire its To Do app at the end of June 2027.

According to recent reports, we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired. But several Microsoft-watching websites this week spotted a blog post from the company recommending people switch to its Planner app.

Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring. For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.

Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. This includes To Do on the web, Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android, for both work or school accounts and personal Microsoft accounts.

The underlying To Do service, APIs, and related synchronization support will retire on separate, later timelines. We’ll communicate those dates and any required preparation separately.

But there’s a big catch for Microsoft customers who are on 365 Personal or 365 Family plans: Planner will not be available to them. That means Microsoft is telling To Do users on those accounts to find a comparable app elsewhere if they’re not on a business account that includes Planner.

The change was also mentioned in a separate Microsoft post about unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365 from Microsoft product manager Ashna Patel.

In a statement provided to CNET, Howard Crow, director of product, agents and AI at Microsoft, said the change consolidates task management across Microsoft 365. “We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare,” Crow said.

Crow mentioned the company will share more information about the transition in the coming months.

While the end of June 2027 may sound like a very long time from now, the path Microsoft has offered for To Do consumers is not a great one if you want to take action now. There’s no built-in export feature in the app, though in the blog post, Microsoft promises, “Microsoft will provide a way to export your To Do data before the apps retire. We’ll update this article with instructions, supported data, requirements, and limitations when those details are finalized.”.

Already, there are some pretty severe limitations even for those on Microsoft plans that support Planner: Existing To Do list items won’t work after that June deadline. “After that date, you will no longer be able to view or manage them in Planner,” the post mentioned.

In the meantime, you can shop around for alternate apps, some free, including Google Keep, ToDoist and Notion.

To Do consumers, myself included, are not happy. As Windows Latest reported, comments in response to Microsoft’s decision included, “Do you actually hate your users?”.

In a recent development, if this were simply a case of Microsoft creating software people didn’t like and then abandoning it, that would be one thing. But the To Do retirement is especially painful for those of us who were forced to move to Microsoft’s app a few years after it purchased Wunderlist.

It has been revealed that wunderlist was a German app that launched in 2011 and swiftly became popular for its slick interface, easy-to-enhancement task lists and its availability across web, desktop and mobile platforms. Microsoft absorbed some of Wunderlist into To Do and killed the original app in 2020 without ever offering all of the features that made Wunderlist great.

Industry observers note that as someone who used Wunderlist for years and has been using To Do, I can tell you that while To Do has been essential in my work and personal life, it never became as intuitive to use as Wunderlist. It never handled predictive task creation as well as Wunderlist did (such as understanding as you typed the date of a task or if it was repeating). It lacked features for sharing lists or collaborating on them, and simply didn’t look as stylish. As far as aesthetics, the best thing Microsoft did with To Do was add a Dark Mode.

Wunderlist was a joy to use. To Do always felt like the knockoff diet version of it and never quite as good.

After several years, I simply gave up on the idea that Microsoft would improve the app or add any fresh features, but kept using it out of necessity given the lack of a built-in export option.

The death announcement is not surprising. Just sad.

RIP To Do, but really RIP to the last remnants of Wunderlist.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.
  • Sources indicate that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found.
  • Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

Sources indicate that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

“Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” noted Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

Around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

It has been revealed that it’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

“We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster remarked.

#222910. Latest Update: We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (933 w)

Latest Update: We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (933 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five years ago, NASA debuted its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed.
  • The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere.
  • At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five years ago, NASA debuted its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed. The mission was a success, making Dimorphos the first celestial object whose orbit was moved by humans. And now, the European Space Agency has published images showing the damage the mission caused to the asteroid.

The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere. The images shown during the livestream were captured by the ESA’s Hera, which was introduced in October 2024 and spent two years in deep space with its two CubeSats to measure, map, probe and eventually land on the asteroid.

At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth. But they were unable to get a good enough view to see how much damage it did to the asteroid or any other potential changes that occurred.

Recent findings suggest that this means that researchers had to estimate the damage until Hera showed scientists exactly what happened. Spoiler: All of those estimates were incorrect, and by a wide margin.

Hera showed the damage was vastly more significant than originally thought. Scientists believed the impact would generate a 20-meter crater; Hera found that almost the entire end of the asteroid had been blown off, resulting in a crater the size of a football stadium and as wide as Dimorphos itself. This is visible in the above image — as you can see, Dimorphos used to be roughly the shape of an egg. Now, it’s the shape of a deviled egg or a kidney bean, depending on which angle you view it from.

Sources indicate that the ESA’s Hera team discovered another neat effect of the impact: Before DART crashed into the asteroid, it was tidally locked to Didymos, much like the moon is to Earth. Scientists expected it to stay that way after the impact, but the images from Hera confirmed that Dimorphos now tumbles randomly, which none of the researchers had on their bingo card.

Industry observers note that “Before the DART impact, Dimorphos has always shown its same face to Didymos,” mentioned ESA Hera Mission Specialist Michael Kueppers during the presentation. “And this is what we see now. You can see it looks for a few seconds in the video like regular rotation, but it’s spinning around completely crazy.”.

ESA mission manager Ian Carnelli said this surprise was great news because it’ll allow Hera to view Dimorphos on all of its sides, which would have been challenging if it were still tidally locked to Didymos.

The ESA concluded the stream with one final surprise. According to Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, the Hera team told engineers that it was entirely safe to go to Dimorphos because all the debris would be ejected from the DART impact, with the remaining bits reabsorbed by Didymos and Dimorphos before Hera arrived.

But there is actually quite a lot of debris around the two asteroids. Kueppers says they’ve identified over 100 boulders so far, marked as white dots in the image above. Despite being completely wrong about the debris field, the Hera team was in good spirits since this means there are more things for the team to study.

According to recent reports, kueppers says scientists are “always happy” either way because when they predict something correctly, they get awarded, and when they predict something wrong, they have a challenge to solve. “The problem is for the engineers,” he noted.

It has been revealed that the three discoveries were made just 20 days into Hera’s mission, which is slated to last six months. The Hera team mentioned more images and discoveries are coming in the next half year.

According to recent reports, the point of the DART mission was to see whether humans could deal with a potentially dangerous asteroid by ramming into it or destroying it, as is often seen in Hollywood films like Deep Impact and Armageddon. NASA even frames it as a “planetary defense test.”.

Industry observers note that the mission was considered an overwhelming success. NASA was hoping to shorten the orbit of Dimorphos by at least 73 seconds, with the most optimal guess being approximately 10 minutes. The orbit was shortened by 33 minutes and 15 seconds. It was such a large discrepancy that scientists studied it and determined that the large amount of debris created extra recoil that amplified the push.

According to recent reports, the change in orbit around Didymos also changed the orbit of both asteroids around the sun by about 11.7 microns per second. This doesn’t seem significant, but it adds up to about 1 kilometer every 2.7 years. This is enough to steer potential city-killer asteroids away from Earth’s orbit, given enough time and a massive enough battering ram.

Sources indicate that hera’s findings also show the impact was much more devastating than scientists first thought. This provides even more data for NASA and the ESA to work through to blueprint for such an event if it ever happens.

“As newly introduced data come in each day, astronomers will be able to better assess whether, and how, a mission like DART could be used in the future to help protect Earth from a collision with an asteroid if we ever discover one headed our way,” mentioned Lori Glaze, director of NASA’s Planetary Science Division, in a statement from 2022.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec. 21, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

    The class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

    The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

    Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

    Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the new devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

    In a recent development, if you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

    “Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our owners,” an Apple spokesperson said in an earlier statement to CNET.

    Recent findings suggest that the court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

    “False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” remarked Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

    Apple lit up its flagship New York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

    As of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the firm Verita directing them to the website.

    The claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

    If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:.

    The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

    It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

    It has been revealed that when Apple advertised its new iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

    According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”.

    Some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

    Industry observers note that according to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

    After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

    On Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

    Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks users do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

    Sources indicate that “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic said.

    In a recent development, artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they update automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free people.

    Anthropic stated the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

    Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

    The revision clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

    “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic said.

    According to recent reports, claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

    The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

    In a recent development, first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid looks, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

    Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

    Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

    Full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic stated, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and update the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

    “Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the organization said.

    For Claude Enterprise plans, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

    3 Lessons From Berkshire Hathaway's Stock Portfolio That Work for Any Stock Portfolio

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • The world is very different now than it was when Warren Buffett first took the helm at Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.12%) back in 1970.
    • For investors who want to distill the Oracle of Omaha's collective wisdom into something simple enough to apply in practice, though, three overarching lessons encompass most of the more detailed tips.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 27, 2026 at 6:51AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    The world is very different now than it was when Warren Buffett first took the helm at Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.12%) back in 1970. However, there's a reason that Berkshire and its stock have continued to perform so well despite never-ending change. That's because Buffett fully understood what really mattered for stocks in the long run, and what didn't. He remained focused on that and ignored the rest. He often even shared these nuggets of wisdom with the rest of the world.

    For investors who want to distill the Oracle of Omaha's collective wisdom into something simple enough to apply in practice, though, three overarching lessons encompass most of the more detailed tips.

    Sources indicate that warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

    Warren Buffett has voiced this idea in a number of ways over the years, such as suggesting you seek out companies with a wide competitive moat, reliable pricing power, and the high profit margins that should be evident with both. Or to put it another way, he argues, "the three most crucial words in investing are 'margin of safety.'".

    In a recent development, the all-encompassing idea, however, is much more direct. Buffett's very first personal rule of investing is "don't lose money," followed closely by the second rule "never forget the first rule.".

    And there's little doubt as to what he meant by it. That is, never put yourself in a position where sizable setbacks can take a permanent toll on your portfolio. While subpar gains are no fun, it's much more difficult to recoup losses than it is to make up for merely below-average performance.

    That doesn't mean Warren Buffett never lost money picking stocks for Berkshire, to be clear. He has. He was one of the key orchestrators of 2015's Kraft-Heinz merger, which turned into a disaster by 2019. Berkshire Hathaway also lost money on its stake in Paramount Global (now Skydance), which it exited in 2024.

    These were legitimate misreads of the two companies' potential (it happens!), not losses suffered simply because Buffett got caught up in hype that was never going to deliver the suggested results.

    It has been revealed that whether they realize it or not, investors who have embraced Warren Buffett's approach to picking stocks aren't merely stepping into specific tickers when they look as if they could move higher. As he penned in 2021's letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders posted in early 2022, "Charlie and I are not stock-pickers; we are business-pickers.".

    According to recent reports, and it's an important distinction to make, if only because it forces you to mentally reframe your stock-picking standards. Given enough time, great businesses will drive their stocks higher simply by creating more long-term shareholder value. Not all stocks racing higher right now will be able to continue rallying, however, simply because their underlying companies aren't capable of sustaining bottom-line growth. It's just fear of missing out that's driving these names up.

    Here's the litmus test: If it were a privately-owned business you were starting or funding on your own, would you be happy with its current, ongoing, and future results for the cost? If not, you probably don't want to become an actual shareholder either.

    It has been revealed that finally, one of Buffett's most important pieces of investing advice isn't actually Buffett's at all. It's Benjamin Graham's, who was one of Warren Buffett's professors while he was a student at Columbia University. It was in Graham's book Security Analysis that he wrote, "In the short run, the market is a voting machine but in the long run it is a weighing machine." This is a crucial truth that allowed Buffett to comfortably ride out the market's rough patches that rattled plenty of other investors out of their stocks at the worst possible time.

    Sources indicate that but what does it mean? "Votes" reflect fickle, ever-changing, short-term emotions. Given enough time, however, stocks will eventually reflect their underlying tech giant's value (which is why you should insist on buying quality companies in the first place).

    According to recent reports, that being said, there's an addendum to this tip. Buffett has also famously said, "Be greedy when others are fearful and fearful when others are greedy." Since fear and greed are emotions -- or "votes" -- that aren't built to last but instead ultimately cede to more sustainable valuations, periods of extreme fear or greed are also buying and selling opportunities, respectively.

    In a recent development, this obviously isn't all of Warren Buffett's body of investing advice. If you can embrace just these three ideas, though, you'll be navigating the market in the same spirit in which he led Berkshire Hathaway to its superior performance.

    #222902. The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (818 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that this was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo.
    • Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter.
    • Industry observers note that the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that this was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo. Notice the lights on the tree, compared to the green hue of the street lighting and blue and pink tones in the sky.

    Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter. The winter solstice is on Dec. 21, when we’ll experience Earth’s shortest, darkest day.

    Industry observers note that the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them. The most common definition, and the one you’re most likely familiar with, is that it denotes the shortest day and longest night of the year on Earth. These times vary depending on your location on the globe, but the further north you live, the less sunlight you’ll get. In the tropics, they’ll get about 12 hours of sunlight. In Sweden, it’ll be closer to 6 hours. In Svalbard, there isn’t any.

    Sources indicate that the reason this occurs is due to the second definition of the winter solstice: During this time, the North Pole is tilted as far away from the sun as it can get. According to The Farmer’s Almanac, the moment at which the Earth’s axis is physically tilted as much as it can be is at 3:50 p.m. ET on Monday, Dec. 21. After that moment, the process will begin to reverse until the South Pole takes its turn during the summer solstice. At that point, the North Pole will be at its closest tilt to the sun, giving us the longest day and shortest night of the year for the Northern Hemisphere.

    Sunset will occur at its earliest time on Dec. 21.

    According to recent reports, it’ll vary by location. The southern US will have the most sunlight, with Florida getting a little over 10 hours during the winter solstice. The Midwest and Great Lakes portion of the country will get roughly nine hours. The Pacific Northwest can expect a little less than nine hours. Southern Alaska will get about six hours, and the northern areas of Alaska will see around three hours.

    In a recent development, if you want to see how your area will fare, Time and Date has a sunrise and sunset tool you can use. Input your zip code into the search bar, and you’ll be able to see your sunrise and sunset times.

    Sources indicate that the city of Utqiaġvik, Alaska, will have it worse than most in the US: It won’t get any sun at all. The sun won’t rise there again until late January. We hope the people living there packed their vitamin D supplements.

    The autumn equinox was just a couple of months ago, so you may be curious about the differences. A solstice occurs when the Earth’s poles are tilted as far away from the sun as they’ll be over the course of one year, which is also one orbit around the sun. The equinoxes take place at the halfway points between each solstice. The autumn equinox takes place in September between the summer and winter solstices, while the spring equinox takes place in March between the winter and summer.

    It has been revealed that during an equinox, the poles are minimally tilted, and the days are as even as they can be. This also has a couple of other interesting side effects: The sun is pointed directly at the equator during an equinox, and the sun will rise and set directly east and west, respectively.

    Humans use the solstices and equinoxes to mark the change of the seasons. There are two equinoxes and two solstices, which mark the start and end dates for Earth’s four seasons.

    Decorating with evergreen trees, like with a wreath, is what they used to do to celebrate the winter solstice.

    While the solstice is close to the holidays, celebrations for the winter solstice have been around for significantly longer, and some winter solstice traditions have become Christmas traditions as well. One of the most historically famous winter solstice celebrations is Yule, a winter festival originating thousands of years ago among the ancient Norse. It became commonly celebrated in Europe and involved bonfires and massive feasts. Yule celebrations also included decorating with evergreen tree decorations, like holly and ivy.

    According to recent reports, if these sound familiar, it’s because Christmas co-opted many of those traditions centuries ago, and the two traditions have kind of merged into a single seasonal holiday. The terms Yule and Christmas are often used interchangeably these days in many cultures.

    In a recent development, so if you want to celebrate the winter solstice, just do all of the stuff you would normally do for the holidays. Burn a Yule log, decorate a tree, eat a big feast with your family and hang up mistletoe and wreaths — those are all hat tips to traditional winter solstice celebrations.

    Breaking: Fast Fashion Fiasco: Shein to Pay $100 Million in FTC Complaint

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (424 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.
    • The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase challenges and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.
    • The complaint also alleges problems with the tech giant’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.

    The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase challenges and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

    The complaint also alleges problems with the tech giant’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.

    “The company misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews,” Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, said in a statement on Tuesday.

    Shein has ballooned over the past decade into the ultra-fast-fashion brand we know today, thanks in large part to the impact influencers have had on social media, posting videos trying on clothing supplied by the tech giant.

    In 2026, the company is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC. That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.

    Recent findings suggest that this isn’t the first time Shein has faced negative scrutiny. Over the years, the company has faced allegations of numerous workers’ rights violations and is the largest polluter in the fast-fashion industry.

    Sources indicate that according to Yale Climate Connections, the organization emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023. Comparatively speaking, that’s more than the pollution output of four coal power plants. Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

    The $100 million will be used to compensate customers. And according to the FTC’s proposed order, the tech giant, which earned roughly $50 billion in revenue in 2025, will not be able to continue advertising inaccurate shipping and delivery times; negative reviews will no longer be hidden; and its customer service offering will be bolstered.

    “The agreement does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices,” a Shein spokesperson told CNET.

    • That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera.
    • Recent findings suggest that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

    That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

    Recent findings suggest that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper stated. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face highlights up and grabs the box.”.

    Package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

    So, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a plan to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

    Cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper said the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

    Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, said Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

    “Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” noted Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”.

    Industry observers note that there are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

    That advice is especially crucial for expensive tech you plan to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

    “While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” said Zackowicz.

    Also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz said.

    If you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can plan accordingly.

    CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

    Regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

    Sources indicate that “The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” said Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”.

    In a recent development, unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

    File a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

    But don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz stated it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

    Recent findings suggest that “Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a newly introduced stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s vital for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” mentioned Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

    In a recent development, after filing, Zakowicz states to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

    Cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

    In a recent development, “I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she said. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”.

    She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

    Industry observers note that cooper claims she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

    Immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who stated it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

    Industry observers note that “I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she said. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”.

    • In a recent development, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.
    • The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee).
    • Recent findings suggest that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two upcoming credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    In a recent development, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    Industry observers note that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for fresh applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    In a recent development, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Recent findings suggest that wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    Sources indicate that with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Latest York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    Recent findings suggest that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    According to recent reports, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    According to recent reports, plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    Sources indicate that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the newly introduced cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    Recent findings suggest that there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s key to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason.
    • From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without.
    • Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research shows thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

    From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

    Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

    According to recent reports, smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you new locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

    Say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

    According to recent reports, video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one reveals up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

    It has been revealed that these advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

    Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

    Package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

    I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

    As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

    Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

    Where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

    These lights also give you phone app controls, which is more important than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

    If you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

    Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    According to recent reports, the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    According to recent reports, securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The manufacturer posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    It has been revealed that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and unveiled the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo noted.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • is home to four publicly listed companies worth $3 trillion or more: Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple.
    • According to recent reports, A high stock price can make it difficult for retail investors to buy into a given company, unless they have access to a broker that offers fractional shares.
    • Meta Platforms (META +3.98%) recently announced a 2-for-1 split, which it will achieve by introducing a new class of shares.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Anthony Di Pizio – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:17AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    In a recent development, the U.S. is home to four publicly listed companies worth $3 trillion or more: Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple. Those companies have created so much long-term value that if they didn't occasionally execute stock splits, their respective share prices would be in the thousands of dollars.

    According to recent reports, A high stock price can make it difficult for retail investors to buy into a given company, unless they have access to a broker that offers fractional shares. A stock split increases the number of shares in circulation, reducing the price per share by a proportionate amount. It's entirely cosmetic, so it doesn't change the value of the underlying company, but it makes the stock far more accessible for small investors.

    Meta Platforms (META +3.98%) recently announced a 2-for-1 split, which it will achieve by introducing a new class of shares. An investor who currently owns one Meta Class A share worth $600 will soon own two shares: one Class A share (with voting rights) and one Class C share (with no voting rights), each worth $300. The split is expected to take effect sometime in January, although the official date is yet to be confirmed.

    Sources indicate that meta has created tremendous value for investors since going public in 2012. Even after accounting for the steep sell-off in the broader market over the past month, the company still has a market capitalization of $1.53 trillion (as of Nov. 25). However, I think it could join the exclusive $3 trillion club within the next few years, giving investors an opportunity to nearly double their money. Here's why.

    According to recent reports, meta is the parent tech giant of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads. During the third quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 30), a whopping 3.64 billion people used at least one of those applications every day. That is a significant portion of the world's population, so it's getting harder for Meta to find new users, especially because its apps are banned in China, which is home to over 1.4 billion people.

    That's why Meta is focusing more on engagement. If each existing user spends more time online, they will see more advertisements, and the company will make more money. Artificial intelligence (AI) is at the center of this strategy, because it helps Meta's recommendation algorithms learn what type of content each user likes to see, so it can show them more of it. The company's chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, said engagement on Facebook and Instagram hit record highs in the third quarter, so the approach is working.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:44 AM ET 11/27/26.

    But thanks to AI, Meta is also penetrating entirely fresh markets outside of social media. The manufacturer introduced a personal AI agent called Muse in September, and it already has over 10 million users. It can perform a range of tasks, but Zuckerberg says one-third of users have deployed it as a personal shopper, with an average purchase size of $200.

    Recent findings suggest that zuckerberg thinks Muse could eventually help billions of people improve their lives, whether they want business advice or tips for healthy living. This will expand Meta's addressable opportunity by potentially taking traffic away from traditional internet search engines like Google Search.

    According to Wall Street's average estimate (provided by Yahoo Finance), Meta is on track to generate $256.9 billion in revenue this year, representing a 27% increase from 2025. Most of that will come from selling ads to businesses on Facebook and Instagram, but Muse gives Meta an opportunity to make money from subscriptions and also transaction fees when the assistant makes purchases. So, it could make a significant contribution to the company's revenue in the future.

    Industry observers note that meta generated earnings of $29.33 per share over the last four quarters, placing its stock at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 20.1. That is a steep discount to the P/E ratio of the Nasdaq-100 index, which is 27.4, suggesting Meta is heavily undervalued compared to a group of America's largest tech companies.

    Moreover, Wall Street predicts Meta will grow its earnings to $33.74 per share in 2027, placing its stock at a forward P/E ratio of 16.6.

    Assuming Wall Street's earnings forecast holds up, Meta stock would have to soar by 64% by the end of next year just to trade in line with the P/E ratio of the Nasdaq-100, which is certainly possible considering its P/E was above 30 for a large portion of the last decade.

    It has been revealed that that gain alone would see Meta's market cap rise to $2.51 trillion, so earnings growth of 19.5% in 2028 would be enough to catapult the manufacturer into the $3 trillion club. Alternatively, earnings growth of just 9.5% in both 2028 and 2029 would produce the same result.

    I say that because slower earnings growth is a real possibility given how much money Meta is spending on AI data centers. It spent $72 billion in 2025 and is on track to spend up to $145 billion in 2026. The manufacturer can't deduct these costs up front because AI infrastructure has a useful life of several years, so it must be depreciated over time instead. That means every dollar spent today could impact Meta's earnings in 2028, 2029, and even 2030.

    Nevertheless, I think Meta has a very high chance of joining the $3 trillion club at some point, even if it takes a little more time than I've outlined.
